signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Carry Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing the 160.00 psychological barrier, trading at 159.96 just below the level that has historically triggered BoJ verbal and physical intervention. While the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage remains the structural driver, the options market is aggressively pricing downside protection with the 25d risk reversal at -1.74 (indicative mid). This strong put skew contrasts with a COT LF net short of -81,619, suggesting professional hedgers are preparing for a policy-driven reversal that futures speculators haven't yet exited. The pair holds above the SMA20 (159.00) and SMA200 (158.42) cluster, but VRP at -1.6% indicates a lack of premium in vanilla options despite the proximity to the intervention zone. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance persists but intervention risk is acute at 160.00. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias remains. Risk: Immediate MoF intervention on a break above 160.00 triggers a disorderly unwind of the -81k spec short position.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5907, with the pair functioning as the primary G10 bilateral theme as the USD leader (1W avg +0.462%) faces the NZD laggard (1W avg -0.417%). Despite the weekly weakness, NZD positioning is at a 52-week extreme with a COT LF net short of -32,496 (pctl 0, z -2.60), creating a massive short-squeeze vulnerability ahead of tomorrow's RBNZ decision. The RBNZ holds a market hike bias, and a 125bp USD/NZD carry advantage is insufficient to justify a record spec short if the central bank delivers a hawkish surprise. Price is currently holding just above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5821–0.5912), suggesting a technical floor is in place. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; record spec shorts are vulnerable to a hawkish RBNZ repricing. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias 100% priced. Risk: RBNZ adopts a dovish hold, validating the record short and pushing price through the 0.5821 support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7167, well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6975–0.7110), but multiple layers signal trend exhaustion. Speculative positioning is crowded with a COT LF net long of +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92), while retail sentiment is at a 88% short extreme, providing a classic institutional-vs-retail divergence. While the 60bp AUD carry advantage supports the pair, WTI crude oil climbing above $86.00 on Middle East tensions introduces a complex geopolitical risk premium that is likely to cap further upside. The negative real rate of -0.55% for the AUD also suggests the RBA is less restrictive than the nominal 4.35% rate implies. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; crowded spec longs and retail fading suggest limited upside momentum. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold bias. Risk: A sharp reversal in crude oil prices triggers a liquidation of the +53k spec long position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — High Volatility Premium + ESI Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3541, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster despite a moderate negative data bias with an ESI of -9.0. The options market is pricing a significant risk premium, with GBP/USD IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 4.9%, resulting in a +6.1% VRP—the highest in the G10 space. This elevated hedging demand suggests institutional players are paying up for protection ahead of the September central bank meetings, even as the spot price remains relatively stable. The Fed-BoE carry spread is currently neutral at 0bp, leaving the pair highly sensitive to shifting US yield dynamics. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional bets expensive. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — hold bias. Risk: A significant beat in UK macro data reverses the -9.0 ESI trend and compresses the vol premium.
